name: mobile-perf-audit-tooling
description: Node-side tooling for the mobile performance audit pipeline (ESLint perf rules, bundle analysis, dependency hygiene, codemod helpers). The pipeline itself is orchestrated from SKILL.md; this manifest only declares the JS-side binaries the worker scripts shell out to.

comments.eslint: Pinned to v8 — v9 flat-config requires plugin updates that several of the react-native / react-perf plugins have not yet shipped. Revisit when those plugins publish v9-compatible majors.
comments.react-perf: eslint-plugin-react-perf catches jsx-no-new-object/array/function-as-prop — the dominant source of avoidable re-renders. Cheap to run, very high signal.
comments.react-hooks: Carries exhaustive-deps + rules-of-hooks. exhaustive-deps in particular surfaces stale-closure bugs that profile traces only show as 'phantom re-renders'.
comments.react-native: Provides no-inline-styles, no-unused-styles, no-raw-text. Inline styles defeat StyleSheet caching; on RN this is a real per-frame cost.
comments.madge: Detects circular imports — these blow up bundle size and break tree-shaking even when the runtime still works.
comments.depcheck: Finds dependencies declared in package.json but never imported. Direct bundle savings on Hermes builds.
comments.knip: Stronger sibling of depcheck — also reports unused exports / files. Run with --no-exit-code so CI does not fail the audit on findings; the audit itself is the consumer.
comments.npm-check-updates: JSON output is folded into facts.json so the report can flag majorly-out-of-date perf-critical deps (RN, Expo, Reanimated, Skia, etc.).
comments.source-map-explorer: Bundle composition. Pipeline runs `expo export` first, then source-map-explorer on the resulting .js + .js.map to attribute bytes per module.
comments.ajv: Used by the synthesize step to validate LLM-emitted prose_fills.json against the slot schema before it ever hits the renderer. JSON-schema in Node has multiple options; ajv is the de-facto standard.
